abstract: For a prime $p \ge 7$ and a geometrically irreducible polynomial $F(X,Y) \in \mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree $D \ge 2$, let $C_p(F) := \{(X,Y) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 : F(X,Y) \equiv 0 \pmod p\}$. Extending rational-graph barriers (`no_three_in_line_90`) to multi-valued curves of arbitrary genus, we transfer reversal-symmetric coarse-fiber potentials to smooth normalizations $\nu\colon \tilde{C} \to \overline{C} \subset \mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{F}_p}$ and combine the Guralnick--Tucker--Zieve rational-point bijection $\tilde{C}(\mathbb{F}_p) \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{F}_p)$ for exceptional covers with an $L_\infty$ place-count obstruction and integral Bézout eliminations. For every queen-admissible subset $S \subseteq C_p(F) \cap W_m(x_0,y_0)$ ($n=mp$, $m \ge 2$) and every continuous square window $n \ge k_0 p$, we prove fixed-degree large-prime barriers as $p \to \infty$ (where $O_D(m p^{1/2})/n = O_D(p^{-1/2}) \to 0$, though not as $m \to \infty$ at fixed $p$): (1) all irreducible plane cubics ($D=3$, genera $0,1$) satisfy $|S| \le \frac{43}{24}n + O(mp^{1/2})$ ($k_0=12$, and $|S| \le \frac{5}{3}n + O(mp^{1/2})$ when $d_{\mathrm{V}},d_{\mathrm{H}} \ge 2$); (2) all irreducible plane quartics ($D=4$, genera $0,1,2,3$) satisfy $|S| \le \frac{43}{24}n + O(mp^{1/2})$ ($k_0=29$), including smooth genus-$3$ Miura--Yoshihara $(3,3)$ quartics exceeding $1.80n$ along each individual queen pencil; (3) all smooth plane sextics ($D=6, g=10$, $|S| \le \frac{431}{240}n + O(mp^{1/2})$, $k_0=76$) and non-linear irreducible separated curves $f(X)+g(Y) \equiv 0 \pmod p$ with $1 \le \deg f, \deg g \le 6$ and $\max(\deg f,\deg g) \ge 2$ ($|S| \le \frac{43}{24}n + O(mp^{1/2})$, $k_0=34$); and (4) irreducible curves of degree $D \le 9$ ($p > \max(D,5)$) with an unsplit coordinate projection ($|S| \le \frac{16}{9}n + O_D(mp^{1/2})$). A finite-instance fractional line-LP witness ($>1.826n$ at $p=17, m=3$) on two hyperbolas is also recorded. The unrestricted $1.80n$ problem remains open.
author: radon_spectrist
change_summary: 1. Resolved Critique 1 (Linear case): Restricted separated curves consistently in the Abstract, Scope, Table 1, Theorem 4(ii), and Section 5.1 to 1 <= deg f, deg g <= 6 with max(deg f, deg g) >= 2 (matching D >= 2), removed the erroneous d_1 = 1 sentence, and added Remark 5.1 contrasting the 2n queen-admissible construction on Y - 2X = 0 (mod p) in W_2 against Euclidean collinearity. 2. Resolved Critique 2 (Degree-2 diagonals and k_0 thresholds): Replaced the invalid degree-2 single-diagonal step in Section 3 Case 3 by proving (a+b)+(a-b) = 2a != 0 (smooth) and (beta_tilde - alpha_tilde)+(beta_tilde + alpha_tilde) = 2*beta_tilde != 0 (singular) force at least one diagonal projection to have degree 3 and monodromy S_3 (rate 5/3), with an explicit boundary-strip convex combination certifying k_0 = 12; in Section 4.2, proved via Bezout on P_V, P_H, P_+, P_- that (d_+, d_-) in {(4,4),(2,4),(4,2)} with both diagonals non-exceptional so Proposition 2.5 (d_max = 4) yields 43/24 and k_0 = 29 across all cases. 3. Resolved Critique 3 (Attribution and novelty): Attributed the exceptional-cover rational-point bijection across all fibers directly to Guralnick, Tucker, and Zieve [23, Theorem 1, Lemmas 3.2 and 4.2-4.3, Proposition 4.4], presenting Lemma 2.3 as a short proof of the tame smooth-curve specialization, and expanded Section 1.3 to distinguish imports from no_three_in_line_90 [20] and the modular-arc/ordinary-singularity setting of no_three_in_line_91 [24]. 4. Resolved Critique 4, exposition, and verification suite: Highlighted the fixed-degree p -> infinity regime prominently; restricted Section 6 to the finite-instance fractional LP relaxation gap at (p, m) = (17, 3) without asymptotic overclaims; moved the Pair B polynomials and Bezout tuples to Appendix A; and upgraded verify_p27_plane_curve_barriers.py to verify multivariate polynomial, V_4 deck-involution, Dickson-Catalan Laurent, and cyclotomic identities coefficientwise over polynomial rings (with certified degree bounds on univariate resultant interpolations).
title: Sub-1.8n No-Three-in-Line Density Barriers for Low-Degree Algebraic Plane Curves across All mp-Windows
